text:
Anna Morgan: Quick check — we're planning a small canary for the Python + TS SDKs in the 18:30 UTC change window. Need final signoff for publish roles, release notes, and whether to include the deprecation blurb for legacy sync client.
Mike Chen: ack. I can own the canary publish + smoke watch. Who's owning docs?
Suresh Patel: I can do the docs update and the deprecation blurb. Will open a tiny PR and link it before canary.
Anna Morgan: thanks. deploy-bot, schedule the canary for 1719805200 and post status here.
deploy-bot: scheduled job #deploy-842 at 1719805200 for packages: @redwood/sdk-python, @redwood/sdk-ts. Canary tag: v2.3.0-rc2-canary. Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/deploy-842 :rocket:
Mike Chen: publishing steps I will run: 
```bash
# build wheels & tgz
make build-sdks
twine upload --repository testpypi dist/redwood_sdk_python-2.3.0rc2.whl
# npm publish for TS to npm-tag canary
cd packages/sdk-ts && npm publish --tag canary
```
Suresh Patel: quick smoke matrix I want run after canary: auth flows, streaming, embedding size sanity, version pin behavior. I can script tests: `scripts/smoke/canary_check.sh`
Ben Ortiz: if we see the ETA token-exchange regression from last week, plan is: 1) yank canary disttag, 2) republish patched wheel with rc2.1, 3) open rollback incident and notify customers. Keep changelog entry ready.
Mike Chen: noted. Rollback checklist condensed: 
- stop traffic to canary route in console
- `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts canary` and `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts previous`
- yank pypi release via admin UI and repush patched wheel with `v2.3.0rc2.1`
- update release notes + customer-facing blurb
Suresh Patel: docs: I will add a short deprecation note for legacy sync client under "Migration" with code example, and a link to the migration script. PR ready in ~20m.
Anna Morgan: question about version pinning: should we recommend `redwood==2.3.*` or pin exact for now? Customers on Dedicated usually want exact pins for repeatability.
Mike Chen: for a GA we recommend exact pin. For canary instruct `==2.3.0rc2` and mention rolling back risks. I'll include that in the release notes template.
deploy-bot: job deploy-842 started at 1719805200. step: build -> success. step: publish -> success for TS canary. Python test upload succeeded to testpypi.
Suresh Patel: running smoke tests now (auth/stream/embed/prompt-format). Posting failures if any.
Mike Chen: tracking here: https://internal/tracking/releases/2.3.0-rc2
Suresh Patel: smoke results: streaming latency ok, embeddings within tolerance, auth token exchange failing intermittently (403 after refresh) — replicable on one host.
Anna Morgan: damn. Mike, hold on further propagation. Can we stop canary routing?
Mike Chen: done — disabled canary route and removed canary npm tag. Commands used: `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts canary` and disabled console routing rule `route: canary-2.3.0`.
deploy-bot: noted: route canary-2.3.0 disabled.
Ben Ortiz: next steps: rollback & republish plan. Who will cut rc2.1? Mike?
Mike Chen: I will cut rc2.1 after we confirm the fix in the auth lib. Targeting republish in 40m.
Suresh Patel: docs/devex note: will add a short "Known issue" line to the release notes and a mitigation for customers using token refresh.
Anna Morgan: thanks everyone. Postmortem of the regression will be short — track it in the release ticket #REL-221. Once rc2.1 is published, we'll run the same canary matrix before GA. :white_check_mark:
